\section[primeiramente]{primeiramente — firstly, first of all}

\label{lesson:PT-C269-primeiramente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for a jungle, then the Portuguese for a slipper.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: primeiramente}
\textbf{primeiramente} — \textquotedblleft{}firstly, first of all\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Primeiramente, abrimos as janelas; depois, limpámos a casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{First of all we opened the windows; then we cleaned the house.}
\end{quote}

A careful word for speeches and written accounts; in speech people usually say \emph{primeiro}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{primeiramente} is built on \emph{primeiro} \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{prīmārius} \textquotedblleft{}of the first rank\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{prīmus} \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with the adverb ending \emph{-mente}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{primeiramente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{primeiramente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{primeiramente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for a jungle, then the Portuguese for a slipper, then say \emph{primeiramente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does primeiramente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Firstly, first of all\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[inicialmente]{inicialmente — initially, at the start}

\label{lesson:PT-C269-inicialmente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for a slipper, then the Portuguese for firstly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: inicialmente}
\textbf{inicialmente} — \textquotedblleft{}initially, at the start\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Inicialmente, ninguém acreditou nele.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Initially, nobody believed him.}
\end{quote}

Tells what was true at the start, before things changed.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{inicialmente} is built on \emph{inicial}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{initiālis} \textquotedblleft{}of the beginning\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{initium} \textquotedblleft{}a beginning\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[seguidamente]{seguidamente — next, then (in a series)}

\label{lesson:PT-C269-seguidamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for firstly, then the Portuguese for initially.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: seguidamente}
\textbf{seguidamente} — \textquotedblleft{}next, then (in a series)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Lavámos os pratos e, seguidamente, fomos dormir.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We washed the dishes and next we went to bed.}
\end{quote}

Formal, common in reports. In everyday talk, \emph{a seguir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{seguidamente} is built on \emph{seguido} \textquotedblleft{}followed\textquotedblright{}, the past participle of \emph{seguir}, which comes from Latin \emph{sequī} \textquotedblleft{}to follow\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\section[posteriormente]{posteriormente — later, subsequently}

\label{lesson:PT-C269-posteriormente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for initially, then the Portuguese for next.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: posteriormente}
\textbf{posteriormente} — \textquotedblleft{}later, subsequently\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O homem foi ao hospital e, posteriormente, voltou para casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The man went to the hospital and later went back home.}
\end{quote}

Formal; you hear it on the news. In speech, \emph{mais tarde} or \emph{depois}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{posteriormente} is built on a Latin comparative, \emph{posterior} \textquotedblleft{}coming after, later\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{post} \textquotedblleft{}after\textquotedblright{}, with the adverb ending \emph{-mente}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[por fim]{por fim — finally, in the end}

\label{lesson:PT-C269-por-fim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for next, then the Portuguese for later.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: por fim}
\textbf{por fim} — \textquotedblleft{}finally, in the end\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Esperámos duas horas e, por fim, o comboio chegou.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We waited two hours and in the end the train arrived.}
\end{quote}

Close to \emph{finalmente}; it closes a list of steps or a story.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fim} is inherited from Latin \emph{fīnis} \textquotedblleft{}boundary, end\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); \emph{por} comes from Latin \emph{pro} \textquotedblleft{}for, in front of\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
